title: [kafka] increase on memory after upgrade clickhouse from version 23.1 to version 23.8.1.2992
body:
Describe the unexpected behavior:

After upgrading ClickHouse from version **23.1**. to version **23.8.1.2992**, we have observed a significant increase in memory usage for our queries. The same queries that used to consume **500 MB** amount of memory on the older version are now using **2,27 GB**  amount of memory on the new version.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Is there a recommended solution, or should I revert to the previous version?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Please provide reproducible example

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
```
create table db.table(
col_1 String,
col_2 Int64,
Time DateTime,
....
col_40
) Engine = replicatedMergeTree('')
Partition by toYYYYMMDD(TIME)
Primary key col_1
order by (col_1,col_2);

```

```
select * 
from ( 
       select col_1 ,col_2 ,col_3 ,col_4 ,col_5 ,col_6 ,col_7 ,col_8 ,col_9 ,
col_10,col_11,col_12,col_13,col_14,col_15,col_16,col_17,col_18,col_19,
col_20,col_21,col_22,col_23,col_24,col_25,col_26,col_27,col_28,col_29

from db.table 
where col_1 in ('value','value','value','value','value' , ... )
and toYYYYMMDD(TIME) between toYYYYMMDD(dataSub(DAY,60 today())) AND toYYYYMMDD(today())

where col_20 <= 100
and col_21 <= 100 
and col_22 <= 100 
and col_23 <= 100
and col_24 <= 100

> try to disable users settings `move_all_conditions_to_prewhere=0` `enable_multiple_prewhere_read_steps=0`

is this the right way to disable it?
`ALTER USER my_user_name SETTINGS move_all_conditions_to_prewhere=0;`


> I see `Peak memory usage: 169.51 MiB.` , but in the first message you reported `are now using 2,27 GB amount of memory on the new version.` ?




I inspected the query_log using the following query:

`SELECT query, memory_usage
FROM system.query_log
WHERE event_date = today() AND normalized_query_hash = 'query_hash_value'
ORDER BY memory_usage DESC
LIMIT 200;
`

This query sorts the results by memory_usage in descending order.
 **I copied the same query that was reported to consume 2 GB.**
 However, when I executed this query manually, 
its memory usage was only around **200 MB.**


Subsequently, I attempted to downgrade to version 23.1, but encountered the following exception:

`DB:exception memory limit exceeded would use 512 TiB (attempt to allocate chunk of 0 bytes)  maximum: 350 GiB 
while executing aggregating transform. (memory_limit exceeded)
`

After encountering this error, I upgraded back to version 23.8.1.2992. The memory_limit_exception ceased, but memory usage is still on the rise.

Now, I'm in a quandary. Downgrading to the older version, which worked well previously, seems problematic. Moreover, I'm uncertain about the potential repercussions if memory usage continues to escalate and reaches its limit.

Thank you for your efforts and expertise as we navigate this challenge. I truly appreciate you taking the time to help.

Somewhere in your configuration file(s) there is "kafka" group.
It is documented here https://clickhouse.com/docs/en/engines/table-engines/integrations/kafka#configuration
Please, add '<kafka.statistics_interval_ms>0</kafka.statistics_interval_ms>' to the group of change the value to '0' if it exists.

So maybe the issue is not related to Kafka, but to insertion in general.

Maybe high insertion rate creates a lot of merges and those merges consume a lot of memory. Could you please check how much memory do the merges use? `SELECT memory_usage FROM system.merges;` and `SELECT sum(memory_usage) FROM system.merges;`.

>At my company we are also seeing this issue, in our case not related to Kafka. It seems that the ClickHouse servers that have more data ingested also tend to have a bigger memory leak. Below is used memory for a sample server with ClickHouse version 23.8.2.7, and the same issue remains with 23.10. After each restart the memory goes down to reasonable levels, and then starts climbing up steadily.

@participant7 This can be tons of things, did you look at the memory distribution inside the server, i.e. something like this?

```sql
WITH
    (SELECT sum(value::UInt64) FROM system.metrics WHERE metric = 'MemoryTracking')               AS memory_tracked_,
    (SELECT sum(total_bytes) FROM system.tables WHERE engine IN ('Join','Memory','Buffer','Set')) AS memory_tables_,
    (SELECT sum(value::UInt64) FROM system.asynchronous_metrics WHERE metric LIKE '%CacheBytes')  AS memory_caches_,
    (SELECT sum(memory_usage::UInt64) FROM system.processes)                                      AS memory_processes_,
    (SELECT sum(memory_usage::UInt64) FROM system.merges)                                         AS memory_merges_,
    (SELECT sum(bytes_allocated) FROM system.dictionaries)                                        AS memory_dictionaries_,
    (SELECT sum(primary_key_bytes_in_memory_allocated) FROM system.parts)                         AS memory_primary_keys_
SELECT
    assumeNotNull(memory_tracked_)                           AS memory_tracked,
    assumeNotNull(memory_tables_)                            AS memory_tables,
    assumeNotNull(memory_caches_)                            AS memory_caches,
    assumeNotNull(memory_processes_)                         AS memory_processes,
    assumeNotNull(memory_merges_)                            AS memory_merges,
    assumeNotNull(memory_dictionaries_)                      AS memory_dictionaries,
    assumeNotNull(memory_primary_keys_)                      AS memory_primary_keys
FORMAT Vertical
```

Maybe this will give some hints (you can also obtain some info like `*CacheBytes` from the `system.asynchronous_metric_log` with the history).

Also does this memory issue arises only *after* upgrade to some version?

P.S. I've just copied this query from the tool I wrote - https://github.com/participant10/chdig/ (since I'm sick of running the same queries over and over again), maybe it will be useful to you as well

comments.author: participant10
comments.body:
Ok, it can be two things then: memory fragmentation and some kind of leak, but I doubt that there is direct leak, though I wouldn't exclude possibility of some live leak.

For memory fragmentation you can take a look at:  `select metric, value from system.asynchronous_metrics where metric like '%jemalloc%'`

As for the leaks:
- at first I would ensure that it is not https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/57822
- then you can look at the following message in the logs `MemoryTracking: was {}, peak {}, free memory in arenas {}, will set to {} (RSS), difference: {}` if the lag is huge, then it means that ClickHouse does not know about this allocations
  - if the answer to previous question is "lag is huge", then you can try jemalloc profiler - https://github.com/jemalloc/jemalloc/wiki/Use-Case%3A-Heap-Profiling (`MALLOC_CONF=prof:true,lg_prof_sample:21,abort_conf:true,confirm_conf:true`)
  - if the lag is is insignificant, then you can try new memory profiler (see `memory_profiler_sample_min_allocation_size` and `memory_profiler_sample_max_allocation_size`), or jemalloc profiler, it will also work great.

After I disabled **statistics_interval_ms**, I restarted ClickHouse 16 hours ago, and everything seemed fine until now. Additionally, I created a new file in **config.d** named **kafka.xml**  then i restarted Clickhouse. 
```
<yandex>
  <kafka>
        <statistics_interval_ms>0</statistics_interval_ms>
  </kafka>
</yandex>
```
I hope this information can assist you.
